subject.title: sandbox: keep workspaceAccess none workspaces writable

question: Should `workspaceAccess: "none"` make the isolated sandbox-owned `/workspace` writable by default while keeping the real agent workspace unmounted?
rationale: The source repro is clear and a maintainer comment points toward isolated-writable `none`, but the change still alters sandbox write authorization and must be accepted as a security boundary before automation implements it.

options.title: Approve Isolated-Writable None
options.body: Treat `none` as no real workspace access rather than no sandbox writes, and require one complete mount/bridge/tool/docs update with live sandbox proof.

options.title: Keep None Read-Only
options.body: Retain the current fail-closed behavior and update docs/support guidance so users choose `rw` or a future explicit writable mode for file-producing workflows.

options.title: Fold Into Bind Policy
options.body: Resolve this together with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/59718 if maintainers want one broader least-privilege write model.

recommendation.title: Approve Isolated-Writable None
recommendation.body: Treat `none` as no real workspace access rather than no sandbox writes, and require one complete mount/bridge/tool/docs update with live sandbox proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The latest maintainer comment on the adjacent strict-gating PR explicitly routes the permanent sandbox contract back to this issue.
